CONTRADICTION FOUND - OUT OF W1 SCOPE, DO NOT CHANGE. D3 clause 3 says 'Projects' is the homeowner-facing tab name in the Patina client app. The shipped tab bar is Today / Spaces / Pieces / Studio; there is no Projects tab. 'Projects' exists only as a screen title one level down (Coordinator.swift:153 AppRoute.projectList displayName 'Projects'), reached from the Studio hub. The Studio tab also uses 'Studio' for the HOMEOWNER's own hub ('Your Studio begins with a project.', StudioHubView.swift:153), which collides with D3 clause 2's 'Studio means the firm'. Resolving this is a separate ticket and needs a ruling on which of the four tabs becomes Projects. It also carries its own analytics-event hazard: AppRoute.studio has its own PostHog screen name, and NounConsistencyTests already pins the rule that the analytics name must not move when the display name does.

D3 clause 1's second half - 'the captured-in-the-field variant -> CapturedPiece' - has no unambiguous target in the code. Everything in apps/mobile/Capture is captured-in-the-field, so a literal reading would make the @Model itself CapturedPiece rather than Piece, contradicting clause 1's first half. This table takes the LITERAL reading of the first clause (Specimen -> Piece) and reserves CapturedPiece as the disambiguating term for the two places where a captured piece must be told apart from a catalog piece: (a) the sibling client app already owns Piece as the marketplace/house noun (PatinaTab.pieces 'Browse pieces', PieceAct, PiecesTabRoot, AppRoute.pieceDetail), and (b) the server's field_captures.capture_kind = 'specimen'. Kody must confirm the reading before W1 renames 1,856 identifiers; if the intent was Specimen -> CapturedPiece, every Piece* row in this table shifts. See lexicon.md section 7.
